title: Cross-surface compatibility policy and staged upgrade orchestration (runtime / API / SDK / Console)
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define a single, cross-surface version compatibility policy and a staged rollout orchestration pattern that covers runtime, public API, official SDKs, and Console. Deliver a support matrix mapping compatibility guarantees per surface and automated tooling and gating rules to run safe upgrades. This ticket collects decisions, implementation acceptance criteria, and rollout runbook for first LTS channel adoption and future major rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Compatibility policy document published and reviewed by Eng/PM/Design/Support
A2: Support matrix spreadsheet covering runtime, API, SDKs, and Console with supported versions and deprecation windows
A3: Rollout gate definitions (canary %, health windows, rollback triggers) implemented in release-controller and Console UI
A4: Upgrade automation prototype (rw-upgrade CLI) that performs preflight checks and orchestrates canary cohorts
A5: Integration tests that validate forward/backward compatibility for KV cache and model artifact formats
A6: Observability dashboards and alerts for canary health (latency P95, token error-rate, throughput drop) defined and wired to runbook
A7: Migration guide and SDK pinning recommendations published to developer docs
steps: S1: Draft compatibility tiers and versioning scheme (semver-like with compatibility labels) and circulate for review
S2: Create support matrix artifact mapping minimum supported runtime, API contract, SDK versions, and Console features per channel
S3: Define staged rollout gates and implement them as policy objects in release-controller (canary percentage, monitoring window, rollback thresholds)
S4: Implement preflight checks in upgrade tooling: schema compatibility, KV cache format checks, kernel capability probe
S5: Wire telemetry for canary cohorts and add dashboards; include synthetic prompt suite and key metrics
S6: Build CLI and Console integration that can schedule a rollout, monitor gates, and perform automated rollback
S7: Run internal dogfooding rollout to validate tooling and matrix, iterate on thresholds and communication paths
S8: Publish public-facing compatibility SLA and migration docs, communicate to SDK maintainers and partners
notes: Decision: Use a compatibility tier model instead of strict semver for the first rollout. Tiers: 'Pin-Exact', 'Compatible', 'Compatible-with-warnings'.
Proposal: LTS channel = 24 months of bugfix + security backports; Stable = 12 months; Fast = 3-6 months. Exact durations to be reviewed by PM/legal.
Upgrade tooling should include a dry-run mode that uses synthetic workloads and validates latency and tokenization consistency before committing canary rollout.
Migration helpers: SDKs will expose 'compatibilityHints' API to detect feature gates at runtime and fallback to safe code paths when interacting with older runtimes.
Backward-compatibility risks: KV cache layout changes and new kernel ops are highest risk. Add feature gates in runtime with opt-in false-by-default behavior for new kernel paths until promoted.
We must ensure model artifact format version is part of the support matrix; older runtimes will be blocked from loading newer artifact versions unless compatibility shim exists.
risks: R1: Insufficient telemetry coverage could cause gates to be blind to regressions (mitigation: synthetic suites + trace sampling)
R2: SDK clients pinned to older API shapes may experience runtime errors; need clear deprecation cadence and migration helpers
R3: Automated rollback may not be safe for stateful customer deployments; include manual approval paths for Dedicated/Private customers
rollout_policy_summary: Gate window: minimum 60m per step (configurable), health checks continuous, rollback on >0.5% absolute error-rate increase or >20% P95 latency regression
Manual holdpoints for Dedicated/Private deployments and configurable customer opt-in for fast channel
observability_requirements: Metric set: request_count, error_count, latency_p50,p95,p99, token_rate, kernel_fallbacks
Alerting: Alert on canary error_rate > baseline + 0.5% and latency_p95 > baseline * 1.2
Tracing: full-span sampling for canary cohorts and error traces enriched with model_version and kernel flags
